problem: fetch_report now passes a caller-supplied URL straight to requests.get. Nothing checks the host or scheme, so callers can make the server request any URL (SSRF).
failure: fetch_report('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/') or fetch_report('http://localhost:6379/') fetches the internal endpoint and returns its body, leaking cloud credentials and internal-only data.
fix: Parse user_url. Require scheme == 'https' and hostname in ALLOWED_HOSTS, and raise ValueError otherwise. Ideally also resolve the host and reject private and link-local IPs.

problem: The diff deletes the ALLOWED_HOSTS allowlist and the urlparse(url).hostname check, and adds nothing in their place.
failure: Before this change, a host outside {api.internal.example, cdn.example} raised ValueError('host not allowed'). Now fetch_report('http://10.0.0.5/admin') raises nothing and returns the response.
fix: Restore ALLOWED_HOSTS and apply the hostname check to the parsed user_url before calling requests.get.

problem: requests.get follows redirects by default (allow_redirects=True). Any hostname check added only at the call site could still be bypassed through a redirect.
failure: An allowed-looking URL that answers 302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/ is followed, and the metadata body is returned.
fix: Pass allow_redirects=False, or re-validate the host on every redirect hop.

problem: The URL scheme is no longer forced to https. Plain http to internal services is allowed, and TLS to the report API is no longer guaranteed.
failure: fetch_report('http://api.internal.example/report') sends the request in cleartext. The old code always built an https://api.internal.example/... URL.
fix: Reject any scheme other than https.

problem: The function keeps its name, but its parameter changes from a relative path to a full URL. Existing callers that pass a path will break.
failure: fetch_report('reports/2026.pdf') now raises requests.exceptions.MissingSchema instead of fetching https://api.internal.example/reports/2026.pdf.
fix: Keep the path-based signature, or rename the function or add a new one and update all callers.

problem: resp.content reads the whole response into memory with no size cap. Now that callers can choose any URL, an attacker can make the server exhaust its memory.
failure: user_url points at an attacker server that slowly streams a multi-GB body. The 10s timeout applies per read, so it never trips, and the worker's memory blows up.
fix: Use stream=True and enforce a maximum byte count while reading. This also needs the host allowlist restored.
